Bicentric Quadrilateral

AlgebraLogic
Game: Move the four dots around the circle and try to make the outside shape fit a circle inside it and a circle around it at the same time.
How to play: Drag a dot with your finger or mouse, or focus the picture, press 1 to 4 and use the arrow keys. Use the button to see the special shape straight away.
Look for the math

Draw four dots on a circle, then draw the tangents where they sit. The four tangents meet in a second, outer quadrilateral. Move the dots: the outer shape changes, but one thing about it never does.

A quadrilateral with two circles

The circle you start with touches all four sides of the outer quadrilateral, so it is an incircle. If the four outer corners also lie on a circle, that is a circumcircle, and the shape is a bicentric quadrilateral. The tangents guarantee the inner circle for every position of the dots.

When does the outer circle appear?

Write the angles of A, B, C, D as a, b, c, d. A dot-product calculation shows the two diagonals AC and BD are perpendicular exactly when a + c - b - d = 180° (mod 360°). In that case the four outer corners are all the same distance from one point, so one circle passes through them all. The logic test checks this over the whole grid of angle choices: the outer shape has a circumcircle precisely in the perpendicular cases, and never otherwise.

Why three points line up

Let I be the centre of the inner circle, E the crossing of the two diagonals (which is also the crossing of AC and BD), and O the centre of the outer circle. When the shape is bicentric these three points are collinear: they lie on one straight line. The column calls the statement projective. The logic test checks it on a large family of right-angle configurations and confirms it; a few symmetric non-right-angle shapes also happen to line up, which the column does not claim against.

The feet of the perpendiculars

Drop perpendiculars from E to AB, BC, CD and DA. Their feet make another quadrilateral KLMN. E is always its incenter: its distance to each of the four sides of KLMN is the same. KLMN becomes a cyclic quadrilateral exactly when ABCD is orthodiagonal — the very same condition as for the outer shape. Both directions were checked exhaustively over the grid of angles.

Press "Make it bicentric", then drag just one dot a little. Watch the outer circle disappear the moment the diagonals stop crossing at right angles.
